title: Forced Ranking Systems and Gender Gaps in Job Tenure
near_miss_reason: Not a controls-only near-miss. Every reported regression is a Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood model (ppmlhdfe), the firm-level abandonment indicator enters only through a female x remove triple interaction (the paper's object is the gender gap, not the main effect), and all columns add individual-level covariates. The exclusions are the nonlinear model and the subgroup-by-treatment interaction, not merely added controls.
eligible_reason: A staggered binary treatment exists (remove = 1 once the employee's company has abandoned its forced ranking system; 13 of 17 firms abandon at 8 distinct years, 4 never do), estimated with company and end-year fixed effects. But no reported specification is a linear TWFE regression of an outcome on that indicator: Tables 4-6 and Figure 1 are ppmlhdfe triple differences (i.female##i.remove) with individual covariates; Figure 2 is a ppmlhdfe event study with female-specific relative-time dummies; Figure 3 randomizes placebo abandonment years. Nonlinear model, subgroup-by-treatment interaction and time-varying controls all fail PROTOCOL.md Section 2.
design_notes: Unit of observation: employee job spell (user_id x position_id) from Revelio Labs online profiles, treated as a repeated cross-section assigned to company_id (17 firms) with time = end_year (year the spell ended; 1979-2023). Outcome job_tenure = months in the position (count). Treatment remove = 1 if the company had abandoned forced ranking by the spell's end year (Empirical_Data.dta); abandonment years from Parallel_Trend_Data.dta rank_end: 2001, 2002, 2012 (2 firms), 2013 (2), 2015 (3), 2017 (2), 2021, 2022; 4 firms never abandon. Table 3: ppmlhdfe job_tenure female + covariates, absorb(end_year company_id [department_id] [state_id]), cluster(end_year). Table 4: same with i.female##i.remove (4 FE variants). Table 5: age subsamples (Empirical_Age_Robust.dta). Table 6: alternative gender-probability cutoffs (Empirical_Gender_Robust.dta). Figure 1: ppmlhdfe DDD on abandoning firms only, margins plot. Figure 2: ppmlhdfe with fpre4-fpre2, fcurrent, fpost1-fpost5 (female x event time, event = end_year - rank_end binned at +/-5; fpre5 and fpre1 dropped) plus male counterparts pre4-pre2, current, post1-post5, absorb(end_year company_id department_id state_id). Figure 3: 1,000 placebo draws of firm abandonment years, ppmlhdfe with female remove_D DDD. Tables 7-9: lab experiment and survey (probit/OLS/ranksum). Standard errors clustered by end_year (about 45 clusters).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 13 of 17 companies abandon forced ranking at 8 distinct years (2001, 2002, 2012, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2021, 2022); 4 companies never abandon. Computed from rank_end in Parallel_Trend_Data.dta.

data_access_note: Regression-ready Stata files for all main-text tables and figures are shipped (README: 'only the data necessary to replicate the main results'); underlying sources are commercial (Revelio Labs profiles, WRDS firm size). Online-appendix data and code are available from the corresponding author.
software_notes: Stata 14 (ppmlhdfe, esttab, coefplot, margins); oTree/Python for the lab experiment.
replication_feasible_note: Package is complete and the Poisson specifications can be rerun, but no reported specification is eligible. A linear TWFE of job_tenure on remove with company and end_year FE could be constructed from Empirical_Data.dta, but it is not a published specification.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Treatment timing verified from Parallel_Trend_Data.dta (rank_end) and from the company x end_year pattern of remove in Empirical_Data.dta. Observation unit is a job spell assigned to its company; the time index is the spell's end year, so the panel is a repeated cross-section of spells rather than a firm-year panel. Clustering is by end_year. Flags in candidates.csv cite Sun-Abraham and Baker-Larcker-Wang, but no modern estimator appears in the code; Figure 3 is a randomization placebo.
